PMID **27509009** — *“Postnatal growth restriction augments oxygen-induced pulmonary hypertension in a neonatal rat model of bronchopulmonary dysplasia”* (2016).

In neonatal rats assessed after 14 days, postnatal growth restriction and 75% oxygen exposure each increased pulmonary arterial pressure, right ventricular hypertrophy (RV/(LV+septum)), and pulmonary arterial medial wall thickness, while decreasing pulmonary vessel number. Combined exposure significantly augmented these changes. The abstract reports no numerical effect sizes.

In a neonatal rat model of bronchopulmonary dysplasia, postnatal growth restriction combined with 75% oxygen exposure for 14 days significantly augmented pulmonary hypertension-related changes, including pulmonary arterial pressure, right ventricular hypertrophy, and pulmonary arterial medial wall thickness; pulmonary vessel number also decreased. The abstract did not provide numerical effect sizes.

Source: PMID 27509009, “Postnatal growth restriction augments oxygen-induced pulmonary hypertension in a neonatal rat model of bronchopulmonary dysplasia” (2016).
